newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Kia Group considers giving up management rights.
newsitem.headline: Kia Group considers giving up management rights.

text.p: The chairman of South Korea's troubled Kia Group was considering submitting to creditor banks a memorandum giving up his management rights, a group spokesman said on Thursday.
He said the group was also thinking of curtailing the number of its executives above the director level by 50 percent.
Earlier this week, it said the group would reduce its executive staff by 30 percent and middle management by 18 percent.
In addition, Kia Group was considering selling its commercial vehicle maker Asia Motors Co Ltd and its sales affiliate Asia Motor Sales Co, he said.
Kia has earlier said it would reduce the number of domestic affiliates to 13 from 28. Selling the additional two units would cut the number to 11.
"The senior management is considering these measures to step up our self-rescue efforts to stay in line with creditors' demands," the spokesman said.
He said it was not known when a decision would be made by the group.
But a source close to Kia Group said these decisions were "inevitable" considering pressures from creditor banks.
Kia had earlier said it would raise 3.1 trillion won by selling real estate, 491.2 billion won by freezing wage increases and 565.3 billion won by cutting production costs and expenditures.
Creditor banks last week selected 18 Kia affiliates for protection after determining the group would be unable to avoid defaulting on its debt payments.
